slides.main: A positive IgG food test mostly shows what you eat regularly.
slides.sub: Which tests actually tell you something, and what to do instead.

slides.main: Allergy societies in Europe and the US advise against IgG food tests.
slides.sub: Many people test positive without any symptoms. Home test kits may also suggest avoiding many foods, which can be harmful.

slides.main: A breath test points to intolerance when symptoms appear during it.
slides.sub: Malabsorbing some lactose or fructose is common and not abnormal in itself.

slides.main: Keep eating gluten before a coeliac test.
slides.sub: NICE advises gluten in more than one meal every day for at least 6 weeks before testing.

slides.main: Cut out one suspected food for a limited time, then bring it back.
slides.sub: A food and symptom diary helps. Don't cut foods out without advice from a GP or dietitian.

slides.main: Get medical help if you have:
items: Symptoms that first started after age 50
Blood in your stool or black stools
Symptoms that wake you up at night
